findings: No new fail-open source defect identified in fixed native request construction, opcode/address/pass discrimination, bounded 523-byte reply assembly, status/extra-data checks or terminal unknown-status behavior.
Physical derivation is compile-only. It checks the fixed real provider hash and snapshot without loading it, pins the tested source and header, and reverses its finite source transformations exactly.

Generated physical executable requires the explicit acquisition flag and exact certificate hash; it locks and hashes the fixed certificate and provider before LoadLibraryExW. No arbitrary provider/kernel/address/opcode argument is exposed.

Physical derivation preserves the compiled protocol payload and ciphertext outside the explicitly replaced provider binding; generated final payload association must be refreshed after any kernel change.
Raw message timestamps/status and bytes are retained in the native journal; no simulated timing is promoted to physical timing.
limits: Read-only source review, no executable, provider, RPC or physical action run by this reviewer.
Fatal native host path deliberately issues no further J2534 calls. Driver cleanup, ECU reset and verified power-loss exit remain external; process termination alone is not cleanup proof.
Host/J2534 echo filtering does not fix ECU SCI self-echo. Attempt03 kernel defect is recorded separately and final communication qualification awaits receiver-control fix.
Certificate/current-ROM identity and physical UART/electrical/adapter acceptance remain separate gates.
